response.markdown_report:
The next experiment should verify that the generated predictor reproduces the selected BERT4Rec checkpoint, supplemented by independently derived fixtures, before changing its learning objective. At 20% progress, this is a feasible prerequisite for interpreting subsequent validation changes; agreement alone can conceal shared implementation bugs.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, all 14,148 audited supervised positions contained MASK, but original corruption provenance was unavailable. Mask presence therefore does not certify event alignment. Second, 800 live identity checks passed. These leave serialization, item mapping and category routing unchecked. Third, substitutions damaged training-prefix recovery more than block swaps. This supports content dependence on those fixtures, without establishing current usefulness or held-out gains.

Three related-work insights identify practical directions. RecTools reserves space for an appended inference MASK, motivating tensor-level comparisons [1]. PyTorch documents restoration, evaluation mode and numerical limitations, motivating separate score and ranking checks [2,6]. Metamorphic testing supplements differential agreement, while mutation research requires verified fault applicability and clean controls [3,7,8].

| Direction | Existing evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision integrity | Consumed-batch reconstruction proposal | Bounded coverage and historical loss capture |
| Deployment consistency | Live identity checks | Actual predictor execution, independent fixtures and catalog filtering |
| Learning alignment | Training recovery sensitivity | Terminal prediction and pinned validation |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Generated-predictor differential audit: 4/8/6.** Originality: connects checks across the actual writer boundary, but testing methods are established. Potential: improves experimental interpretability, but parity cannot itself improve ranking. Difficulty: no network changes, but independent fixtures, routing, process isolation and catalog checks require substantial integration [1–3,6–9].
- **Fixed terminal-mask training mixture: 4/8/4.** Originality: adapts a known objective mismatch, but terminal masking is established. Potential: may improve inference alignment, but benchmark gains remain unknown. Difficulty: localized sampling changes, but normalization and target-event exclusion require care [4].
- **Interior–terminal gradient comparison: 5/6/6.** Originality: adapts gradient-conflict analysis, but cosine disagreement is familiar. Potential: may localize interference, but cannot establish harmful transfer. Difficulty: reuses one network, but extra backward passes consume budget [5].

Select the differential audit, retaining terminal-mask training as the next learning experiment. Freeze small training-history fixture suites covering empty, short, full-length and repeated histories. Independently specify expected mapping, truncation, padding, MASK placement and readout; never derive these expectations through production preprocessing. Compare the live selected checkpoint with the actual generated `working/predict.py` in an isolated process, including ordered external candidates, configuration, strict loading, routing, available intermediate tensors and final recommendations.

Match inference precision and runtime settings. Predeclare score tolerances; separately report score error, top-k membership and order, highlighting near ties. Check candidate/batch permutations, duplicate candidates and chunked versus unchunked raw catalog scores. For the twenty designated training users, exclude publicly observed seen items and PAD/MASK without changing pinned benchmark eligibility.

Calibrate copied-artifact wrong-route and wrong-readout faults using verified execution and changed intermediates; retain independently checked clean controls. Report denominators, surviving faults and unavailable checks. Preserve one checkpoint/category and diagnosis interfaces. Only pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 selects revisions. Fixtures can be overfit through adaptive debugging; freeze a final check suite and log changes. No parity or accuracy gain has been measured.

idea.description: Add a bounded differential audit comparing the selected live BERT4Rec model with the actual generated working/predict.py loading the exact same category checkpoint, supplemented by independently derived preprocessing fixtures, applicable metamorphic relations, and verified fault controls.
idea.motivation: Consumed-batch provenance and live-module identity checks leave export, serialization, item mapping, routing and full-catalog recommendation behavior uncertified. Differential agreement can also conceal shared bugs. Independent discrete expectations and bounded deployment checks make subsequent sampler and loss experiments more interpretable without adding another trained predictor or claiming recommendation gains.
idea.implementation_notes:
This remains an integration proposal because the baseline trainer, predictor writer and callable prediction interface were not supplied. Exercise the actual generated predictor through its production entry point in an isolated process; do not substitute a reference predictor that bypasses the writer. Observe the actual training-side inference path rather than rebuilding that path inside the audit. If invocation or observation support is absent, return null with a reason. End-to-end outputs can still be checked when intermediate hooks are unavailable, but missing internals cannot count as passed.

Freeze a small fixture manifest before execution using only supplied training histories, mappings and catalog information. Record exact fixture histories, ordered external candidates, category, expected discrete fields, selection rules, manifest version and checkpoint identity. Cover empty, short, unequal-left-padding, maximum-length, truncation-boundary and repeated-item histories. Derive expected token sequences and mapping round trips independently of production preprocessing. Empty-history behavior must follow an explicit supported contract; otherwise mark that fixture unsupported. Use synthetic mapping/unit fixtures only for discrete logic where needed, clearly separate from scored real-history fixtures. Never read validation or test histories to manufacture fixtures.

Golden fixtures validate specified discrete behavior, not exact neural scores. Require exact equality for IDs, token sequences and applicable masks. Reserve one position for MASK, retain the last L-1 history events, left-pad, append the reserved MASK and read its greatest nonpadding absolute position, never count-1. A repeated target item in earlier history is legitimate. Compare positional IDs and attention masks when exposed, without assuming arbitrary padding shifts preserve representations with absolute positional embeddings. Check external-ID round trips, category-local mapping identity, saved architecture configuration and strict state-dict loading. Include categories with overlapping local IDs to detect route confusion. Strict loading alone cannot detect a semantically incorrect same-shaped configuration. Use checkpoint and mapping identities plus observed routing; do not introduce additional fitted checkpoints.

Match model implementation, candidate order, batch shapes, device, software versions, evaluation mode, dtype, autocast and TF32 settings across processes. Record these settings in the manifest. For the diagnostic FP32 reference, disable autocast and TF32 using APIs supported by the installed PyTorch version; do not mix incompatible precision-control APIs. Enable deterministic algorithms where supported and set process-local randomness without changing training RNG. Report unsupported deterministic operations as explicit limitations rather than silently falling back. If the deployed predictor normally uses another precision policy, exercise that actual policy separately; diagnostic reference agreement cannot certify an untested deployment mode. Restore every module's prior mode, global main-process RNG and modified backend settings in finally. Process-local determinism does not imply cross-platform reproducibility.

Predeclare FP32 score tolerances of rtol=1.3e-6 and atol=1e-5 for matched reference executions. Any other supported dtype requires its own justified tolerance declared before results. Record maximum absolute error, relative error with an explicit denominator convention, nonfinite counts and the tested score count. Do not widen tolerances after failures without recording a protocol revision and retaining the original outcome. Compare candidate-aligned raw scores, top-k membership, ordered external IDs and auxiliary-fixture hit decisions separately. The score-closeness bound is atol + rtol*abs(reference), not a ranking guarantee. With epsilon equal to the observed maximum candidate-wise absolute discrepancy, reference score gaps greater than 2*epsilon protect pairwise order; a k/k+1 gap greater than 2*epsilon protects top-k membership for the same eligible set. Report boundary gaps and near-tie changes without changing the pinned evaluator's ranking rule. Training-fixture hit decisions are recovery diagnostics, not validation measurements.

Check candidate permutation, duplicated-candidate equality, batch permutation, isolated-versus-batched requests and save/reload relations only where the production API supports them. Use matched shapes for direct parity, then report shape-changing relations separately because numerical kernels can differ. For independently implemented diagnostic top-k merging, break exact ties by a declared stable external-ID order; compare production outputs under the production tie rule and expose any mismatch. Do not impose this diagnostic tie rule on the host evaluator.

Audit full-catalog unseen-item recommendations separately from the sampled-candidate benchmark. For the twenty designated training users, five/category, explicitly exclude PAD, MASK and all publicly observed seen items available for that request. Do not read hidden interactions or change pinned benchmark eligibility. Encode a history once and score eligible real items in bounded chunks using the exact trained scoring head and its output transformation, including a bias if the actual architecture has one. Never add a bias solely because a reference implementation uses one. Merge raw logits globally; independently normalized chunk probabilities are not comparable. Compare chunked and unchunked scores and rankings on bounded feasible catalog fixtures, covering chunk boundaries and nearly exhausted unseen catalogs. Return fewer than k recommendations when fewer eligible items exist; never refill with seen or reserved tokens. Verify final external IDs, uniqueness and routing. If unchunked checking exceeds the predeclared memory budget, report unavailable coverage rather than claiming full-catalog parity.

Calibrate on isolated copied artifacts only, never during training or checkpoint selection. Wrong-route mutants must reach a compatible route and demonstrate a changed mapping, checkpoint selection or another asserted intermediate; a shape error alone tests rejection, not silent routing detection. Wrong-readout mutants require unequal-left-padding fixtures on which count-1 differs from the final MASK position and the mutant actually executes. Independently verify applicability, changed intermediates and non-equivalence relative to the asserted contract before counting a mutation in detection coverage. Do not require a changed final ranking when the corrupted intermediate itself violates an asserted property. Record attempted, inapplicable, invalid, equivalent, unresolved, verified non-equivalent, detected and surviving cases with reasons. Report detection coverage over verified applicable non-equivalent mutants, null for zero denominator. Run identical checks on independently verified unchanged and harmless controls; report clean-control failures separately. Restore copied artifacts exactly and verify restoration. Mutation survival is neither proof of equivalence nor evidence of real-world fault prevalence.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView hooks: view.model is the actual nn.Module, with item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Return metrics and metric_definitions with assertion-specific denominators, failures, unavailable reasons and artifact references. Preserve existing family-safe diagnostics using captured replay records or a disposable diagnostic iterator; never advance the production loader. Main-process RNG restoration does not restore worker-local state or iterator progress. Require explicit runner and manifest transport rather than assuming host hooks exist.

Keep supervision-integrity auditing, deployment consistency, training-exposed recovery, gradient correctness, convergence, qualitative feedback and host validation distinct. Passing deployment checks cannot establish source-label integrity, causal recency, choose-now usefulness or absence of popularity shortcuts. Only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are available; item categories, review content, ratings, commercial attributes and simulator traits remain unavailable. No explanatory fluency or simulated judgment supplies preference ground truth. No additional learned scorer is fitted.

Preserve four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per completed epoch. Keep single-GPU execution and exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint per category. Live/reloaded executions and diagnostic copies use that same checkpoint and are never fused, averaged or independently optimized. Preserve the twenty designated users' full-catalog recommendations. Do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Checkpoint configuration and the embedded predictor writer remain consistent; any future inference change must update the writer.

Bound fixture counts, process launches, catalog-check sizes, mutation cases and execution time before running; record overhead within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Group requests by category to avoid unnecessary repeated reloads. Freeze a separate final fixture suite before debugging where feasible, retain original failures and log assertion/protocol adaptations. Such a suite limits test-specific debugging overfit but provides no held-out accuracy estimate. Only pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 selects model revisions. Keep terminal-mask mixture training as the next feasible learning experiment after auditing, rather than expanding diagnostic scope indefinitely.
idea.pseudocode:
def audit_generated_predictor(view, runner, manifest, fixtures):
    if runner is None or manifest is None:
        return unavailable_with_definition('Actual predictor runner or manifest missing')
    state = capture_module_modes_rng_and_backend_settings()
    try:
        configure_declared_reference_inference()
        view.model.eval()
        rows = []
        # Expectations were independently authored before production execution.
        for category_fixtures in group_by_category(fixtures):
            exported = runner.launch_actual_generated_predictor(
                path='working/predict.py',
                checkpoint=manifest.selected_checkpoint(category_fixtures.category),
                settings=manifest.reference_settings)
            for fixture in category_fixtures:
                live = observe_actual_training_side_prediction(view, fixture)
                deployed = exported.observe_prediction(fixture)
                rows += check_independent_discrete_expectations(
                    fixture.golden_fields, live, deployed,
                    unavailable_fields_are_not_passes=True)
                rows += compare_checkpoint_config_mapping_and_route(
                    live, deployed, manifest)
                rows += compare_aligned_raw_scores(
                    live, deployed, rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5,
                    reject_nonfinite=True)
                rows += compare_membership_order_and_boundary_gaps(
                    live, deployed, preserve_production_tie_rule=True)
                rows += check_supported_metamorphic_relations(
                    exported, fixture,
                    relations=['candidate_permutation', 'duplicate_candidates',
                               'batch_permutation', 'isolated_vs_batched'])
            rows += bounded_catalog_checks(
                exported, category_fixtures,
                use_actual_scoring_head=True,
                compare_raw_chunked_and_unchunked_scores=True,
                exclude_public_seen_and_reserved=True,
                verify_external_ids_and_global_topk=True)
            exported.close()
        controls = []
        for operator in ['wrong_category_route', 'count_minus_one_readout']:
            for fixture in predefined_mutation_fixtures(fixtures, operator):
                mutant = mutate_isolated_copy(operator, fixture, manifest)
                status = independently_verify_reachability_and_changed_contract(
                    mutant, fixture, operator)
                controls.append(classify_and_test_mutant_only_if_verified(status, mutant))
                verify_exact_restoration(mutant)
        controls += run_identical_checks_on_verified_clean_and_harmless_controls()
        return summarize_metrics_definitions_counts_failures_and_unavailable(
            rows, controls, manifest, include_runtime=True)
    finally:
        restore_module_modes_rng_and_backend_settings(state)

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Use captured replay or an explicitly disposable diagnostic loader.
        result = existing_family_safe_diagnostics_without_production_iteration(
            self.view, train_loader)
        audit = audit_generated_predictor(
            self.view, explicit_optional_actual_predictor_runner(),
            explicit_selected_checkpoint_manifest(),
            frozen_training_only_fixtures_with_independent_expectations())
        merge_metrics_and_definitions(result, audit)
        return result  # {'metrics': ..., 'metric_definitions': ...}

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis,
        include=['measured_metrics', 'definitions', 'denominators',
                 'failures', 'unavailable_reasons', 'protocol_adaptations'],
        distinguish=['supervision_integrity', 'deployment_consistency',
                     'training_recovery', 'qualitative_feedback', 'host_validation'],
        prohibit=['unmeasured_passes', 'invented_accuracy_gains',
                  'causal_preference_claims', 'ensembles'])

originality.positive: Connects event-level integrity work to the actual predictor writer, independent preprocessing fixtures, category routing and catalog recommendation boundary under BERT4Rec semantics.
originality.negative: Differential testing, golden fixtures, metamorphic relations and mutation controls are established techniques; the contribution is task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides reusable deployment evidence for subsequent architecture, sampling and objective experiments while reducing ambiguity about exported behavior.
future_potential.negative: Passing bounded checks neither certifies all execution paths nor improves recommendation relevance; excessive auditing could delay the terminal-mask learning experiment.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no new learned parameters, training objective or independently fitted scorer, and bounded fixtures limit computation.
code_difficulty.negative: An actual predictor runner, independent expectations, precision controls, verified mutations, mapping and routing checks, and catalog parity make the previous rating of 5 optimistic.

related_work.title: [1] RecTools BERT4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for left padding, history truncation and appended-MASK inference.
limitations: Does not establish correctness or parity of the host implementation; expectations must follow the supplied model's actual contract.

related_work.title: [2] PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents state-dict restoration and evaluation-mode requirements.
limitations: Successful parameter restoration alone does not verify preprocessing, semantic configuration, item mapping or category routing.

related_work.title: [3] Model-level metamorphic-testing research (supplied search result)
contributions: Motivates checking equivalent executions through predefined metamorphic relations.
limitations: BERT4Rec relations require task-specific applicability checks; arbitrary padding shifts need not preserve absolute-position representations.

related_work.title: [4] Recency Sampling for Neural Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Identifies weak correspondence between masked reconstruction and terminal next-item prediction.
limitations: Does not establish that a terminal-mask mixture improves the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: [5] Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Provides a framework for examining conflicting objective gradients.
limitations: Interior–terminal BERT4Rec gradient comparisons are a proposed adaptation; disagreement alone does not demonstrate harmful transfer.

related_work.title: [6] PyTorch numerical accuracy and score comparison
contributions: Explains numerical differences associated with precision settings, platforms and mathematically equivalent computations.
Supports recording runtime settings and separating score closeness from ranking preservation.
limitations: Deterministic execution does not guarantee cross-platform equality; numerical guidance does not supply a universal application tolerance.

related_work.title: [7] ML classifier metamorphic-testing study (supplied search result)
contributions: Supports using applicable metamorphic relations to identify implementation faults that ordinary predictive evaluation can miss.
limitations: Classifier findings do not validate the proposed BERT4Rec relations or replace independently derived preprocessing expectations.

related_work.title: [8] Reachable-mutant study and critical reflection on ML mutation testing
contributions: Motivates verifying that mutations reach applicable execution paths and change relevant intermediate behavior.
The accompanying supplied critical reflection, https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01341, motivates explicit treatment of mutation realism and test-versus-production behavior.
limitations: Synthetic fault detection does not estimate production fault prevalence.
Surviving mutations require separate analysis of equivalence, applicability and unspecified behavior.

related_work.title: [9] RecBole BERT4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides a reference for appended-mask prediction and consistent candidate/full-catalog scoring using the model's scoring head.
limitations: Its padding and indexing conventions must not be copied into this left-padded task.
A scoring bias or other architectural feature should be checked only when present in the actual trained model.

related_work.title: [10] RecBole ID mapping and recommendation utilities
contributions: Provides implementation context for external-ID conversion and recommendation eligibility filtering.
Dataset mapping documentation is available at https://recbole.io/docs/recbole/recbole.data.dataset.dataset.html.
limitations: Sequential recommendation paths can differ in history filtering; unseen-item eligibility must be specified explicitly for this task.
These utilities do not determine the pinned host evaluator's eligibility or tie handling.

related_work.title: [11] PyTorch deterministic algorithms, autocast and assert_close
contributions: Documents score comparison using absolute and relative tolerances, including FP32 defaults.
limitations: Score tolerance is not a ranking guarantee.
APIs and supported deterministic operations depend on the installed version; runtime settings must be recorded and checked.
